referenceFunction.generalComment:
Direct Air Capture (DAC) of CO2 through temperature-vacuum swing adsorption. This DAC process uses adsorbents to capture CO2 from the air and separates it through vacuum and low-temperature heating. Climeworks provides data from its commercial DAC plants, which consist of multiple CO2 collectors and heat exchangers, capturing and releasing CO2 in cyclic operations. The solid sorbent used here is Amine on Silica. It can be regenerated at low temperatures (80-120C). For the sorbent system, the LCI data are collected from the work of Deutz and Bardow based on the Climeworks system. The LCI data represent a plant with an annual capacity of 100 kt CO2/year and a lifetime of 20 years.
Source: Deutz, S., Bardow, A. Life-cycle assessment of an industrial direct air capture process based on temperature-vacuum swing adsorption. Nat Energy 6, (2021). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-020-00771-9. Assumes "future" electricity consumption of 0.5 kWh/kg CO2 captured as per Deutz and Bardow, 2021. Current electricity consumption is closer to 0.7 kWh/kg CO2 captured. Future heat demand is 5.4 MJ/kg CO2 captured, as per Deutz and Bardow, 2021. The current demand is closer to 11.9. Future MEA consumption is 3 kg/t CO2 captured. Current consumption is closer to 7 kg/t CO2 captured, as per Deutz and Bardow, 2021. UUID: bf3edfd6-d2bc-3885-8acb-5c718d43ae2d
